Concerns.Title: East of the Well
Concerns.Pitch: Sit down a minute. You'll have heard the saying; the children skip to it. Don't go east-of-the-well after dark, you might not come back you. Well, the lamps out east of the well have gone dark, every one, and nobody's walked over to fill them. Three flasks of lamp oil would do it, and somebody's legs. Then there's the wall. People chalk their names there so the east knows who they are, and somebody ought to read them out loud, every name. I won't. The lamp-man won't. The lamp-man's wife won't, and she isn't afraid of anything: not geese, not him, not the dark.
Concerns.Thanks: There. That's done. Don't tell me about it. Thank you. I'll not ask how.

Approaches.Label: Bring three flasks of lamp oil for the lamps east of the well.
Approaches.Objective: Bring Slip's warden three flasks of lamp oil

Approaches.Label: Read the names chalked on the east wall, out loud.
Approaches.Objective: Read out the names on Slip's east wall

Refusal.Text: I won't go east of the well. I'm saying it now, to your face.
Refusal.Reply: Nobody blames you. Chalk your own name up before you leave, though. Everybody does.
